unclassified.reason: the other ~32KB. This is a boot-path map: 22 routines out of a 32768-byte ROM. Anything not named below is unanalysed, not empty.

RAM, not ROM: the byte the M88 comparison harness fingerprints. It is game-specific (for many titles the keyboard-scan gate) and its meaning in the ROM has never been established — 0xFF is not necessarily "stuck", several titles hold it there in M88 too.

a lead that did NOT pan out. At frame 80 this address writes CD FF 00 (CALL 00FFh) into C444 while executing from inside the F000-FFFF text-VRAM window (tools/watch-write.mjs). It was pursued as the root cause of the Makaimura divergence; the real cause turned out to be the missing uPD765 MT (multi-track) feature. Kept because the observation is real and the interpretation was wrong — exactly the pair this format keeps together.

evidence.basis: tools/watch-write.mjs at f80; retracted as a cause in docs/m88-comparison.md

notes:
Scope: how the main CPU talks to the FDD sub board and reaches a disk boot. 6F06-780A are in the main ROM image (verified: n88.rom holds CD 51 45 1C at 6F06, matching the vector-call form) even though the N88 extension ROM banks over 6000-7FFF when selected — read the bank state before trusting an address in that window.

Confidence mapping: as in the sub-board document, romlabels.js "verified" becomes `inferred` here because no occurrence count survives from those sessions.

ROM revision, measured 2026-08-10: this FR n88.rom differs from the m88204 set's n88.rom in 18 of 32768 bytes, at 322E-3232, 3C08-3C0E, 79D7 and 7C5F-7C63. None of them falls inside a routine named below, so these labels happen to survive the swap — "happen to" being the entire argument for romHash. The same set's Pc88.rom differs from its own n88.rom in 107 bytes, which is how two emulators ended up running different revisions of the same ROM without anyone noticing (docs/m88-comparison.md).
